summary: Allow an authenticated SaaS tenant user to securely connect a global OIDC sign-in provider from the profile sign-in methods panel.
userImpact: Existing SaaS users can connect Microsoft or another configured global OIDC provider after proving control of their current EnterpriseGlue account.
A connected global provider can be used for later Cloud sign-ins without enabling email-only account merging.
configuration: Global-provider account linking is available only when pooled tenancy and Cloud account identity are both enabled.

changes: The authenticated identity-provider list now includes sanitized global OIDC providers that are eligible for explicit account linking.
The existing authenticated OIDC link endpoint accepts an exact configured global provider while retaining its tenant-session binding.

notes: The existing global external-identity records store the new subject binding; no schema migration is required.

security: The link remains bound to the current non-revoked user session, active tenant, exact provider ID and key, provider callback, signed short-lived state, browser state cookie, and PKCE verifier.
Provider email must match the authenticated account, and an external subject already owned by another account remains rejected.
The change does not enable pooled verified-email auto-linking and does not grant tenant authorization from global provider claims.
Provider configuration and credentials are never returned by the self-service provider list.
documentation: Generated release documentation records the secure global SaaS OIDC account-link flow and its trust boundary.
knownLimitations: Global providers are presented as explicit reconnect actions because tenant-scoped profile reads intentionally cannot inspect global external-identity rows through tenant RLS.
Self-service linking remains limited to direct OIDC providers; SAML and LDAP linking remain outside this flow.
rollback: Roll back the host release to remove global providers from the authenticated link surface; already-created valid external-identity links remain usable and can be unlinked through existing administration controls.
validation: Focused signed-state, OIDC route, provider-provisioning, identity contract, authorization-structure, protocol-rehearsal, typecheck, package-discipline, and release-note checks.
Protected CI and a staging Microsoft account-link and subsequent sign-in browser pass are required before accepting the release.
